items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: And Louis Katzman, who was a conductor very good one I'll never forget. He says, man, if this guy doesn't show up. I says, look, I'll do it on sax.

ctx.x: Sure. The rage flag. Well, this actually happened. I was working on a small radio station in New York, 1934 and 35. And we had an orchestra of about 10 men. Trumpet, three saxes, violin, cello. And this one night, every night we used to do Empire Gold or something. But before that there was a rave track call, done live by the trumpet player. The trumpet player was late. And Louis Katzman, who was a conductor very good one I'll never forget. He says, man, if this guy doesn't show up. I says, look, I'll do it on…

I think, you know, you had so many years of experience with Paul Whiteman, starting with Toscanini. Right. Why don't you people ask some questions? He has some terrific stories. We just came off of a radio show with Roy Roberts on WSMB, what, an hour or two ago? Oh, 11 to 1131. You know, the nut to nut and stuff sort of thing. And yesterday we were on WWL. And Mr. Gavro has some marvelous things, stories that will help you even musically. Yes. Sure. So why don't you fire away? Start with the Paul Whiteman area if…
